rated.sentence: One thing I would separate out before choosing a Stocky replacement is what you actually need Stocky for.
Some stores mainly need purchase orders and receiving.
Some need inventory counts and barcode workflows.
Some need forecasting/replenishment.

For apparel stores, I think the forecasting part is usually where generic tools get messy, because the real issue is not “the hoodie is low”, it is “Medium / Black is low while other sizes are still fine.”
So I would make a quick list of:
Do you need POs/receiving?
Do you need multi-location transfers?
Do you need variant-level reorder forecasting?
Do you need barcode stock counts?
If variant-level forecasting is the main problem, I built a small Shopify app called Restocked for that exact use case: reorder risk by size/color variant for apparel/accessory stores.
It is not a full ERP or full Stocky replacement, but it may fit stores that mainly need a clearer reorder list.

For multi-store and marketplace sync, use a few representative SKUs and test whether an order, refund, cancellation, and manual adjustment update every relevant location quickly enough to prevent oversells.

For replenishment, test whether the tool produces a reviewable reorder list from sales, stock on hand, lead times, and safety stock, then lets you turn that list into a PO you can check before exporting.
That makes it easier to see whether one tool genuinely fits both jobs or whether sync and purchasing need separate tools.

It supports the planning side with reorder recommendations and supplier purchase orders that can be exported as Excel files.
